claims.text: The premelting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by surface-to-volume ratio.
The melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by surface-to-volume ratio.
A higher surface-to-volume ratio increases the influence of surface energy on thermal stability and phase transitions.
Systematically changing nanoparticle size changes the surface-to-volume ratio.
High-entropy-alloy composition causes surface energy and lattice strain.
Smaller nanoparticles have increased surface energy and lattice strain.
Increased surface energy and lattice strain lower nanoparticle thermal stability.
Smaller high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles premelt at lower temperatures than bulk material or larger nanoparticles.
Smaller high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles melt at lower temperatures than larger nanoparticles of the same composition.
Bulk high-entropy alloys and large nanoparticles have minimal surface effects relative to smaller nanoparticles.
The proposed size effect should hold from a few nanometers to several hundred nanometers.
Surface effects remain significant over the stated range from a few nanometers to several hundred nanometers.
The relationship between surface-to-volume ratio and thermal stability may depend on alloy composition.
The relationship between surface-to-volume ratio and thermal stability may depend on defects or impurities.
